The Hero Killer.text: Stain, called the Hero Killer by the press and the police, is the most wanted villain in Japan. Working alone, he has killed or crippled dozens of pro heroes across several cities, and as of the start of the year he has never been caught. His pattern is known from survivors and case files: he watches a city's heroes from its rooftops, chooses one, strikes at night in a narrow place, and is gone before backup arrives. He fights with knives and a sword. Survivors report that after the first cut they could not move, and police files hold no confirmed account of his Quirk. Survivors also say he calls his victims fakes, and investigators read his creed in his choices: a hero who works for money, fame or a ranking is a fraud, a true hero acts only to save others, and the fakes must be purged until the word hero means something again. Sightings describe a lean man with a scarred face, a long tattered red scarf and a cloth bandana, too few to give the public a clear picture. Detectives in several prefectures share his files, and the Hero Public Safety Commission reviews them with the police. Every new attack dents public trust in heroes and puts agencies on edge: pros double up on night patrols where they can, and talk shows argue over whether the system that ranks heroes by popularity created him. To most of the public he is a name on the news and a reason to be glad of a hero nearby.
